family: 2D grid and matrix operations (transpose, neighbours, path counts, flood fill sizes)
spec: Given a 2D grid (a list of lists of integers), return its transpose, a new grid where rows and columns are swapped. The input grid may be rectangular (m rows by n columns) rather than square, and the result must have n rows and m columns. If the grid has no rows, or its rows are all empty, return an empty list.

family: 2D grid and matrix operations (transpose, neighbours, path counts, flood fill sizes)
spec: Given a 2D grid of integers, return a new grid representing the original rotated 90 degrees clockwise. The grid may be rectangular; if the input has m rows and n columns, the output must have n rows and m columns. Return an empty list if the input grid is empty or has no columns.

family: 2D grid and matrix operations (transpose, neighbours, path counts, flood fill sizes)
spec: Given a 2D grid of integers, return a new grid representing the original rotated 90 degrees counterclockwise. The grid may be rectangular; if the input has m rows and n columns, the output must have n rows and m columns. Return an empty list if the input grid is empty or has no columns.

family: 2D grid and matrix operations (transpose, neighbours, path counts, flood fill sizes)
spec: Given a 2D grid of integers, return a new grid representing the original rotated 180 degrees (equivalent to reversing the order of the rows and reversing each row). The grid may be any size, including a single row, a single column, or empty, in which case an empty grid is returned.
reference:
def rotate_180(grid):
    return [row[::-1] for row in grid[::-1]]

family: 2D grid and matrix operations (transpose, neighbours, path counts, flood fill sizes)
spec: Given a 2D grid of integers, return a list containing the sum of each row, in order from the first row to the last. Rows may contain negative numbers or zeros, and if the grid has no rows return an empty list.
reference:
def row_sums(grid):
    return [sum(row) for row in grid]

family: 2D grid and matrix operations (transpose, neighbours, path counts, flood fill sizes)
spec: Given a 2D grid of integers with at least one row (all rows the same length), return a list containing the sum of each column, in order from the first column to the last. If the grid is empty or its rows are empty, return an empty list.

family: 2D grid and matrix operations (transpose, neighbours, path counts, flood fill sizes)
spec: Given a 2D grid of integers, a row index r, a column index c, and a target value, count how many of the (up to four) orthogonal neighbours of cell (r, c) - above, below, left, and right - are within the bounds of the grid and equal to the target value. Cells on an edge or corner simply have fewer neighbours to check.

family: 2D grid and matrix operations (transpose, neighbours, path counts, flood fill sizes)
spec: Given a 2D grid containing only the integers 0 and 1, find the size of the largest group of 1-cells that are connected to each other horizontally or vertically (not diagonally). If the grid contains no 1-cells at all, or the grid is empty, return 0.

family: 2D grid and matrix operations (transpose, neighbours, path counts, flood fill sizes)
spec: Given a 2D grid of integers, return a list of the elements on its main diagonal, that is grid[0][0], grid[1][1], grid[2][2], and so on, stopping once either the rows or the columns run out. The grid need not be square. Return an empty list if the grid is empty or has no columns.

family: 2D grid and matrix operations (transpose, neighbours, path counts, flood fill sizes)
spec: Given a 2D grid of integers, return a list of the elements on its anti-diagonal, running from the top-right corner to the bottom-left, that is grid[0][cols-1], grid[1][cols-2], and so on, stopping once either the rows or the columns run out. The grid need not be square. Return an empty list if the grid is empty or has no columns.

family: 2D grid and matrix operations (transpose, neighbours, path counts, flood fill sizes)
spec: Given a 2D grid of integers, return a list of its elements visited in clockwise spiral order, starting at the top-left corner: across the top row, down the right column, back across the bottom row, up the left column, and then spiraling inward, repeating until every cell has been visited exactly once. Return an empty list if the grid is empty or has no columns.

family: 2D grid and matrix operations (transpose, neighbours, path counts, flood fill sizes)
spec: Given a 2D grid whose cells are strings, and a target string value, count how many cells in the entire grid are equal to that value. If the grid is empty, or the value never appears, return 0.
reference:
def count_value_occurrences(grid, value):
    return sum(row.count(value) for row in grid)

family: 2D grid and matrix operations (transpose, neighbours, path counts, flood fill sizes)
spec: Given a 2D grid of integers, return a list of the values of all the cells that lie on the border of the grid (the first row, the last row, the first column, or the last column), listed in row-major order (row by row, left to right within each row). If the grid has only one row or one column, every cell is a border cell. Return an empty list if the grid is empty or has no columns.

family: 2D grid and matrix operations (transpose, neighbours, path counts, flood fill sizes)
spec: Given two 2D grids of integers, determine whether the second grid can be obtained from the first by rotating it by 0, 90, 180, or 270 degrees. Return True if any of those four rotations of the first grid equals the second grid exactly (same dimensions and same values in the same positions), and False otherwise. Two empty grids are considered equal.

family: 2D grid and matrix operations (transpose, neighbours, path counts, flood fill sizes)
spec: Given a 2D grid of integers, return a single flat list containing all of its elements in row-major order (the first row's elements in order, then the second row's, and so on). If the grid has no rows, or all rows are empty, return an empty list.
reference:
def flatten_grid(grid):
    return [x for row in grid for x in row]

family: 2D grid and matrix operations (transpose, neighbours, path counts, flood fill sizes)
spec: Given a 2D grid of integers, possibly containing negative numbers, return the sum of every element in the grid. If the grid has no rows, or all rows are empty, return 0.
reference:
def grid_sum(grid):
    return sum(sum(row) for row in grid)

family: 2D grid and matrix operations (transpose, neighbours, path counts, flood fill sizes)
spec: Given a non-empty 2D grid of integers with at least one cell, return a tuple (row, col) giving the position of the maximum value in the grid. If the maximum value occurs more than once, return the position of its first occurrence when scanning row by row, left to right.

family: 2D grid and matrix operations (transpose, neighbours, path counts, flood fill sizes)
spec: Given a 2D grid of integers, determine whether it is symmetric, meaning it equals its own transpose (grid[i][j] == grid[j][i] for every valid i and j). A grid that is not square (different number of rows and columns) is never symmetric. An empty grid (no rows) counts as symmetric.

family: 2D grid and matrix operations (transpose, neighbours, path counts, flood fill sizes)
spec: Given a non-empty 2D grid of integers where every row has at least one element, return the index of the row whose elements sum to the largest total. If more than one row ties for the largest sum, return the smallest such index.

family: 2D grid and matrix operations (transpose, neighbours, path counts, flood fill sizes)
spec: Given a non-empty 2D grid of integers with at least one column, return the index of the column whose elements sum to the largest total. If more than one column ties for the largest sum, return the smallest such index.
